study: Agentic verification study: the origin of Arm C
design: Pre-specified paired comparison: one run per arm on the same claims and retrieved passages; primary comparison C against B1R, pre-specified alpha 0.05

dataset.name: SciFact DEV (claims_dev.jsonl)
dataset.gold_label_rule: a claim's unanimous rationale label: SUPPORT gives SUPPORTED, CONTRADICT gives CONTRADICTED; claims without evidence have no gold label
dataset.previously_used: These claims had been used by earlier project systems, so they are not an untouched test set.

metric.primary: two-class macro-F1 (SUPPORTED, CONTRADICTED) over all 188 labelled claims; INSUFFICIENT and failed outputs count as errors
metric.false_support: gold CONTRADICTED claims predicted SUPPORTED, out of 64
metric.no_evidence_committed: claims without gold evidence on which the arm still decided SUPPORTED or CONTRADICTED, out of 112

statistics.permutation: two-sided paired sign-flip test, 10,000 permutations, seed 20261022, p = (b+1)/(B+1)
statistics.bootstrap: paired percentile bootstrap of the macro-F1 difference, 10,000 resamples, seed 20261023
statistics.mcnemar: exact two-sided McNemar test on claims only one arm got right (secondary, uncorrected)
statistics.unpaired_arm_intervals: per-arm percentile bootstrap, 10,000 resamples, seed 7; computed for the write-up, not pre-specified

B1.definition: One verifier pass judges each of the top 8 retrieved passages; the claim is decided only when the passages that take a side agree, otherwise INSUFFICIENT

B1R.definition: B1's recorded outputs with a rank tie-break: when the passages conflict, the best-ranked passage that takes a side decides (primary baseline, protocol amendment A1)

C0.definition: B1, then, when B1 is undecided, an adjudicator decides from the passages that took a side; an unusable adjudication falls back to the rank tie-break. No search

C.definition: C0, plus a planner that writes up to 2 further retrieval queries over the SciFact corpus when no passage takes a side; new passages are judged before adjudication (Arm C)

posthoc_studio_rules.what: arm_c_studio's rules 1 and 2 applied to the recorded Arm C outputs of this study: no model was run
posthoc_studio_rules.status: Post-hoc and exploratory: the rules were chosen after these records were examined. It re-decides old outputs on previously used claims. It is not a measurement of arm_c_studio, which works on web evidence and has not been evaluated.

verification.method: Recomputed by the project with a standard-library re-scorer that does not use the study's own scoring code, from minimal per-claim records (claim id, prediction, passage ranks and stance labels; no text) and the official SciFact claims_dev.jsonl
verification.result: 10 of 10 published figures matched exactly at their published precision; 79 of 79 further values agreed with the study's recorded aggregate results
verification.public_recomputation: Not possible yet. The per-claim records and the re-scorer are withheld while the SciFact licence terms are clarified (the dataset's GitHub licence file and its Hugging Face card state different licences).

does_not_establish: the accuracy of the current Research Studio or its default verifier arm_c_studio
a statistically significant improvement over the B1R baseline (p = 0.081; the interval includes zero)
performance on fresh, unseen claims: the DEV claims had been used before
performance with web evidence, other models or other domains
stability across repeated runs: one run per arm
